newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Santos stevedores reach agreement with Cosipa.
newsitem.headline: Santos stevedores reach agreement with Cosipa.

text.p: Stevedores at Brazil's Santos port have reached an agreement with steel firm Companhia Siderurgica Paulista (Cosipa) to continue sharing loading and unloading at its terminal, a union official said.
"The stevedores will continue working there for six months," Antonio Pinho, second secretary of the Santos Stevedores' Union, said after a union assembly.

Cosipa offered on Tuesday night to continue the work-sharing regime which has been in place since April, when stevedores staged two strikes in protest at the firm's decision to use only its own workers at its private terminal, Pinho said.
Cosipa officials were not immediately available to confirm the agreement.

The company last week said talks with unions had failed and announced it would begin using its own workers on an exclusive basis from Aug 4, a move which shipping agents feared could cause a fresh strike.
Pinho said new talks may be held later in the year to determine whether stevedores should have a right to handle 100 percent of the cargo at Cosipa's terminal.
